title: Potential lack of lawful basis for health data sharing
description: Wearable device may share sensitive health data (exercise sessions, GPS traces) without adequate legal basis or user consent
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if proper consent mechanisms are in place for health data processing

title: Sensitive health data exposure
description: GPS traces and exercise sessions could reveal sensitive health information about the user, potentially enabling health profiling

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Sensor data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during the sync process

title: Unintended data exposure during sync
description: Data could be exposed to unintended recipients during the sync process, including potential metadata leakage

title: Potential unauthorized data disclosure
description: Companion app may disclose user data to third parties (e.g., advertisers, data brokers) without user consent

title: User behavior profiling
description: App could use exercise and GPS data to build detailed user profiles for targeted advertising or behavioral analysis

title: User's health data linked to personal identity
description: User's calorie, meal, and weight data could be used to identify and profile the user, potentially revealing sensitive health information that could be misused for discrimination or targeted advertising.
assumptions: User voluntarily shares data but may not fully understand implications of identity linking

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: User's sensitive health data (calories, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through the companion app or its service providers.
assumptions: Data sharing occurs through app infrastructure that may have third-party connections

title: Unintended consequences of data sharing
description: User may not be aware of all potential consequences of sharing health data, including how it could be used for insurance, employment, or other purposes.
assumptions: User provides informed consent but may not fully understand downstream uses

title: Data flow metadata reveals user identity
description: Meta-data about the data flow (timing, frequency, volume) could be used to link the user to their health activities and potentially identify them.
assumptions: Data flow metadata is captured and potentially analyzed

title: App disclosure of user health data to third parties
description: Companion app may disclose user's health data to third-party service providers, advertisers, or data brokers without explicit consent.
assumptions: App has access to user data and may share it with external parties

title: Inadequate data destruction by app
description: Companion app may not properly destroy user's health data when account is deleted or when data retention period expires.
assumptions: App has data retention policies that may not include proper destruction

title: Location tracking through health data
description: App could infer user's location or movement patterns from the timing and frequency of health data entries.
assumptions: Data flow timing and patterns could reveal location information

title: Inappropriate User Identification
description: The mobile app may collect and transmit more identifying information than necessary for the health logging functionality, potentially including device identifiers, location data, or other personal information beyond calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects minimal required data for health logging purposes

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app may disclose health log data to third parties (e.g., advertisers, data brokers, or other services) without explicit user consent or appropriate privacy controls.
assumptions: Assumes the app has mechanisms to control third-party data sharing

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The mobile app may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) regarding health data collection, storage, and transmission, potentially resulting in legal and regulatory penalties.
assumptions: Assumes the app operates in jurisdictions with privacy regulations

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Health log data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) may be intercepted during transmission from the mobile app to the health log store, especially if the communication channel is not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow uses standard network transmission

title: Unauthorized Data Access at Destination
description: The health log store may grant unauthorized access to health log data to third parties, administrators, or other users without proper authentication and authorization controls.
assumptions: Assumes the data store has appropriate access control mechanisms

title: Improper Data Destruction
description: The health log store may not properly destroy or anonymize health log data when requested by users or when data retention policies expire, potentially leading to data breaches or privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes the data store has data retention and destruction policies

title: Unintended Location Tracking
description: The mobile app collects and shares GPS location traces with timestamps, which can be used to track individual movement patterns and infer sensitive information about the user's daily activities, habits, and whereabouts.
assumptions: Assumes the app has access to GPS sensors and can transmit location data without user consent or awareness.

title: Individual Identification via Location Data
description: Location traces with timestamps can be used to identify and track specific individuals, potentially revealing personal routines, home/work locations, and sensitive places visited.
assumptions: Assumes location data is unique enough to identify individuals and can be linked to specific users.

title: Unintended Disclosure During Transmission
description: Location data in transit between the mobile app and location history store could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may not be fully secured.

title: Location Data Storage and Retention
description: The location history store retains GPS traces with timestamps, creating a persistent record of user movement that could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for long-term tracking.
assumptions: Assumes the store retains data for extended periods without proper deletion mechanisms.

title: Location Data Used for Identification
description: The location history store may use stored location data to identify and profile users, potentially creating detailed movement profiles that reveal sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the store has mechanisms to link location data to user identities.

title: Unintended Access to Stored Location Data
description: Location data stored in the location history store could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns and personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the store has appropriate access controls that may not be fully effective.

title: Lawful basis for data sharing unclear
description: The health log store may share calorie, weight, and exercise data without a clear lawful basis or appropriate legal justification for the analytics service to access this sensitive health information.

title: Insufficient notice about data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their health logs will be shared with the analytics service for health-condition analysis, violating transparency requirements.

title: Data interception during transit
description: Health data in transit between the health log store and analytics service could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive calorie, weight, and exercise information.

title: Unintended use of health data
description: The analytics service may use the health logs for purposes beyond the stated health-condition analysis, such as commercial profiling, insurance underwriting, or third-party sharing without consent.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: The analytics service may disclose the aggregated or individual health data to unauthorized third parties without proper authorization or user consent.

title: Processing without adequate safeguards
description: The analytics service may process sensitive health data without implementing appropriate technical and organizational safeguards required by privacy regulations.

title: Location data sharing without consent
description: Location history data is shared from the data store to analytics service without explicit user consent, potentially violating privacy expectations around location tracking.
assumptions: Users may not be aware their location history is being accessed for analytics purposes.

title: Location data enables individual identification
description: Location history data can be used to identify and track specific individuals, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about their movements and habits.
assumptions: Location patterns are unique enough to identify individuals.

title: Location data interception during transmission
description: Location history data in transit between data store and analytics service could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately encrypted or protected.

title: Location pattern analysis reveals sensitive information
description: The analytics service derives daily routine and movement patterns from location data, which could reveal sensitive information about user habits, health status, or personal activities.
assumptions: Movement patterns can be correlated with sensitive personal information.

title: Analytics service identifies individuals from location patterns
description: The health analytics service may use location pattern analysis to identify and profile specific individuals, potentially creating detailed personal profiles.
assumptions: Location patterns are distinctive enough for individual identification.

title: Location analytics data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Processed location analytics data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent.
assumptions: Data sharing controls may not be adequate.

title: Insufficient legal basis for data sharing
description: The Health Analytics Service may share inferred health insights without a clear legal basis or adequate consent from users, potentially violating data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates under data protection regulations requiring lawful basis for data processing.

title: Inaccurate or misleading inferred insights
description: The inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags may be inaccurate or misleading, potentially causing users to make incorrect health decisions based on flawed analytics.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics algorithms may have limitations or errors in their inference capabilities.

title: Insufficient notification of data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately notified about the specific inferred insights being shared with the Companion Mobile App, limiting their ability to exercise privacy rights.
assumptions: Assumes notification requirements exist for data sharing between services.

title: Data flow metadata exposure
description: Meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them may be exposed during data transmission, potentially enabling correlation attacks between the analytics service and app users.
assumptions: Assumes data flow metadata may contain identifying information about the parties involved.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health insights
description: The Companion Mobile App may disclose the received health insights to third parties without proper authorization or user consent.
assumptions: Assumes the app may have access to third-party sharing mechanisms.

title: Unintended use of health insights
description: The Companion Mobile App may use the received health insights in ways not intended by the user or the original analytics service, potentially leading to privacy concerns.
assumptions: Assumes the app may have broader functionality than initially disclosed.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: The app may share sensitive health information (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) with unauthorized parties or share more data than necessary for the intended purpose.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Sensitive health data transmitted from the app to the user could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.

title: User inadvertently disclosing sensitive information
description: The user may inadvertently disclose sensitive health information to unauthorized parties through their actions or interactions with the app.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Data at Cloud Provider
description: The third-party cloud hosting provider may have unauthorized access to the sensitive health and location data, models, and analytics data stored on their infrastructure, potentially leading to data breaches and privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate security controls in place, but third-party access risks remain.

title: Data Loss at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may experience data loss due to technical failures, natural disasters, or other incidents affecting their infrastructure, resulting in loss of the health and location datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has disaster recovery and backup mechanisms, but data loss remains a risk.

title: Data Interception During Transit
description: The analytics data, models, and health/location datasets may be intercepted during transmission from the Health Analytics Service to the Cloud Hosting Provider, potentially exposing sensitive information.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over networks that may not be fully secured, though encryption is typically used.

title: Loss of Confidentiality at Source
description: The Health Analytics Service may share sensitive health and location data with the third-party cloud provider without adequate confidentiality protections, potentially leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the source has some control over data sharing practices, but third-party access creates confidentiality risks.
